extracted.intended_audience: ecology researchers who submit preprints or act as reviewers/recommenders/data editors for PCI Ecology (authors, reviewers, recommenders, journal editors, and data/code editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for submitting, reviewing, recommending, and publishing ecology preprints via the Peer Community In (PCI) Ecology platform, including editorial policies and data/code quality control guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public recommendation and publication pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints positively evaluated by PCI Ecology are publicly recommended and can be published directly in Peer Community Journal, or can be submitted to PCI-friendly journals or other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation by PCI Ecology is a public endorsement that enables (but does not force) direct publication in Peer Community Journal or submission to journals that accept PCI-recommended preprints; authors should consult PCI-friendly journals list for options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read guides and editorial policies before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a preprint, please carefully read the guide for authors, PCI Ecology's community-developed editorial policies, and find out what you can do with a PCI Ecology-recommended preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to consult the guide for authors and editorial policies to ensure submissions meet format, scope, and procedural requirements; failure to follow these resources may delay or preclude consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission eligibility and article types
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept most types of articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although PCI Ecology accepts most article types, authors should check thematic fields, submission procedures (including B2J direct submission from bioRxiv), and any field-specific guidance in the guide for authors to ensure fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code availability, functionality, and metadata (SORTEE guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that data and code are available, code runs properly and data is in the appropriate format and has the corresponding metadata to be scrutinised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The role of data editors is not to verify correctness but to ensure availability/usability: include runnable code, standardized data formats, clear metadata, and follow the SORTEE six-step recommendations from basic requirements to gold-standard reproducibility; provide instructions so data editors and readers can run analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of data editors (scope of checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data editors ensure that data and code are available, code runs properly and data is in appropriate format with metadata, but are not responsible for verifying the actual data and code correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear expectations: data editors check availability, reproducibility (code runs on provided data), and metadata completeness, but do not perform substantive validation of analytical correctness or scientific interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should provide clear presentation of methods, intuitive explanations of key equations, and clear definitions of objectives and terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers valued clarity improvements such as clearer presentation of statistical results, more intuitive explanations of key equations, and better definitions of main objectives/terminology; authors should prioritise readability and transparency of analytical steps so readers and reviewers can assess methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sensitivity analyses and explicitly acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sensitivity analyses and more explicitly acknowledge important ecological and methodological limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity analyses and explicit limitation statements strengthen manuscripts by showing robustness to assumptions and clarifying the scope of inference; reviewers have requested these as part of revisions and considered them important for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate sampling design and complementary methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use complementary sampling techniques and a well-structured dataset to capture the phenomena under study (e.g., combining hand netting and pan traps for pollinator studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching sampling methods to ecological questions and reporting complementarity/limitations of methods improves confidence in results; reviewers note when studies use multiple methods and assess how each contributes to inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overinterpretation; cautious inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be careful not to overinterpret findings given data limitations and should avoid overstating conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers favour conservative interpretation: where data are limited (e.g., small sample sizes, few events), explicitly state uncertainty, alternative explanations, and avoid strong causal claims unsupported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, timeliness, and conceptual contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are assessed for novelty, timeliness, and whether they advance methods or understanding in ecology (e.g., mapping relationships between estimators, proposing new frameworks bridging correlative and mechanistic approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation decisions weigh whether the manuscript provides new insights, connections between methods, timely solutions to open problems, or clear advances in applicability; reviewers highlight novelty and potential to stimulate follow-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and applicability to applied contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the applied value and potential for implementation (e.g., conservation planning tools, management trade-offs, policy relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts that bridge theory and practice or provide tractable tools for applied use are highly valued; reviewers often comment on management implications and practical applicability as part of recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and model adequacy, assumptions, and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods (statistical models, simulations) must be appropriate, with clear discussion of assumptions, model performance, and potential extensions or generalisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect discussion of when model assumptions hold or fail, comparisons to alternative approaches, and plans for future generalisations; presenting simulation evidence about model behaviour and limits is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear presentation of results, including statistical outputs and a well-structured discussion placing findings in broader context, is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements requested during peer review frequently include clearer presentation of statistical results, expanded discussion of ecological and management implications, and better articulation of how results fit with existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship/contribution and licensing for published texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright under CC BY for texts published after 24/01/2022 and under CC-BY-ND before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be aware of the copyright and licensing terms that apply to texts they submit to PCI Ecology (affects reuse and derivative works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/procedural options (submission routes and roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct submissions to PCI Ecology from bioRxiv.org are possible using the B2J service; interested researchers can sign up to review or contact to become recommenders; journal editors can pursue PCI-friendly arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use provided submission routes (e.g., B2J) if applicable; reviewers/recommenders should follow platform procedures (create account, sign up) and contact the managing board for recommender appointments or journal liaison.
